subject: P95 & throughput dip for MattressCo — mitigation options and customer note
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-07T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Observed P95 jump + throughput dip affecting MattressCo (NYC region)

Team — quick heads-up. We’re seeing a sustained P95 latency increase and a drop in throughput for MattressCo in the us-east-1 region starting ~08:30 PST. Snapshot attached. Key numbers:
- P95 gen latency: baseline ~180ms -> current ~860ms (x4.8)
- Average throughput for their tenant: -31% last 90m
- Error rate is nominal; tail retry volume up ~12%

Initial signal points to increased KV-cache churn correlated with a model variant rollout performed ~07:45. I’m investigating whether tokenizer behavior or sequence-length distribution changed, leading to worse cache hit rates.

Immediate asks:
1) Product: do we want to rollback routing for MattressCo to the previous model/variant or accept a temporary degraded-performance variant?
2) Eng/SRE: fastest mitigations you can implement (route pin, emergency caching param, per-customer rate cap) and estimated time-to-fix.
3) CS: draft a short customer-facing note so we can notify MattressCo if we need to apply a mitigation that impacts latency/throughput.

Attaching: latency-snapshot-20281107.png

– Diego
Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-07T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observed P95 jump + throughput dip affecting MattressCo (NYC region)

Thanks Diego — good catch. A few clarifying questions:
- Was MattressCo pinned to the new variant explicitly, or were they routed by policy?
- Any sign the model itself changed tokenization (i.e., different tokenizer file)?

High-level product ask: minimize customer-facing disruption. If we can switch MattressCo to the previous variant for a short rollback (with no schema changes), that’s preferable. If rollback risks regressions for other customers, consider a per-tenant routing override + brief maintenance window notification.

Also: if the mitigation requires disabling certain batching optimizations or enabling a quantized fallback, we should list the expected delta in latency and throughput so CS can set expectations.

Marissa
Director, Product — Serving

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-07T10:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observed P95 jump + throughput dip affecting MattressCo (NYC region)

Update after deeper triage and a quick heap/profile:
- Cause hypothesis: model rollout introduced an updated tokenizer mapping (small change in byte-pair merges). That produced different chunk boundaries and KV cache keys, causing effective cache miss rate to spike for sessions pinned to the new variant.
- Evidence: cache hit-rate for that model bucket fell from 92% -> 54% across affected hosts; tokenization length distribution shows +18% longer average sequence for the same prompts.

Mitigations available now (with quick ETA):
A) Route MattressCo back to previous model variant (m-redwood-v3) — ETA 12–25 minutes to validate and rollout per-tenant override. Minimal risk; preserves throughput.
B) Enable quantized fallback variant (m-redwood-q3) for MattressCo — ETA 8–15 minutes; expected p95 ~+40–80ms vs pre-incident, but throughput should recover. Slight quality delta, we should flag QA risk.
C) Apply temporary per-tenant rate shaping (throttle new sessions) — ETA 3–7 minutes; avoids rollback but reduces client throughput while we stabilize.

I can implement (A) immediately if product signs off. Otherwise (B) is fastest with a clear communicated quality trade-off.

– Diego

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-07T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observed P95 jump + throughput dip affecting MattressCo (NYC region)

Agree with Diego. Operational notes if we pick option A (rollback route):
- We'll need to patch the routing table for MattressCo and prime the KV cache (warmup) by replaying recent sample requests — warmup adds ~10–15 minutes but avoids the initial cold misses.
- I'll own validation steps and can run the rollback during the next 30–45min window. Minimal code change; config-only.
- If we pick B, engineering will run quick A/B validation against a canary to confirm quality delta <2% on Rouge/trace metrics.

Recommend: Product signoff for (A) + CS customer note before change.

Ben
Engineering Manager — Inference Runtime

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-07T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: DRAFT customer message for MattressCo — please review

Hi Liam / Sandy —

We wanted to alert you to a performance issue that affected your account in the NYC region this morning. Our engineering team observed elevated latency and a temporary drop in throughput beginning at ~08:30 PST. We’ve identified a root cause related to a model variant rollout that changed tokenization behavior for a subset of requests, and we are implementing a targeted fix to restore normal performance.

Planned action (pending your acknowledgement):
• We will revert your traffic to the previous model variant for the next 45 minutes to ensure cache stability and throughput recovery. This is a targeted, non-disruptive routing change that preserves the response quality you had prior to the rollout.
• If you prefer not to revert, we can instead switch you to a quantized fallback variant which is faster to enable but may have small differences in output.

Expected customer impact: brief maintenance window (~20–45 minutes) during which some in-flight requests may experience retries; overall throughput should return to normal. We’re offering a one-time service credit for the impacted window — happy to confirm details with contracts if you’d like.

Please reply with your preference (revert or fallback) and we’ll proceed immediately. Apologies for the interruption and thanks for the patience.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

[attachment: draft-mattressco-note-v1.docx]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@mat-co.com>, Sandy Park <sandy.park@mat-co.com>, contracts@mat-co.com
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-09T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: P95 & throughput dip for MattressCo — mitigation options and customer note

Liam / Sandy — following our internal triage, we propose the following immediate action to restore consistent performance for MattressCo: revert your traffic to the previous model variant for a short stabilization window. This is the least-risk option and should bring throughput and tail latency back to expected levels within ~30 minutes.

If you approve, we will:
• Schedule the revert to m-redwood-v3 now and begin a cache warm-up sequence; expected stabilization ~20–40 minutes.
• Monitor closely and provide an update when the P95 returns to baseline.
• Issue a one-time service credit for the impacted period; contracts@mat-co.com, please advise how you’d like us to proceed on the credit paperwork.

If you prefer the quantized fallback instead, let us know and we’ll roll that as an alternative — that path is slightly faster to enable but may show small quality differences in a minority of prompts.

We aim to proceed within the next 10 minutes if we don’t hear back. Apologies for the disruption and thanks for your quick reply.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Technical Account Lead — Redwood Inference
